llm_output.why_top_candidate_wins: Chile Influenza Activity has the strongest and most direct evidence linking it to the failure: it is the only candidate that (1) is a documented LEADING_INDICATOR_FOR the failed target signal (signal_us_hosp) and (2) has both an IMPORTATION_LINK and a POSSIBLE_DRIVER_OF relationship to the US mechanism (eq_us_flu_base). Those three supporting edges together give it a higher score (7) and provide two independent pathways by which Chile activity could cause an underpredicted, missed peak in US hospitalizations (direct lead indicator of the target and mechanistic connections into the model). The other candidates lack this full set of supporting edges (Australia lacks an importation link; Travel Importation Pressure lacks a direct leading-indicator edge to the target), making them less plausible given the observed failure and ranking.
llm_output.proposed_minimal_edit: Add a single mechanistic term linking lagged Chile influenza activity into the US mechanism: introduce an importation-driven seeding/forcing parameter in eq_us_flu_base that is modulated by signal_chile_flu (e.g., add a term + beta_chile * lag(signal_chile_flu, k) to the force-of-infection or importation rate). Test fitting beta_chile (and a small lag k) while keeping other model structure unchanged.
llm_output.caveat: This recommendation is based solely on the provided support subgraph and candidate ranking; it does not incorporate external epidemiological data, travel volumes, or model diagnostics. The suggested edit assumes the graph edges reflect real temporal and mechanistic relationships that warrant a lagged importation/forcing term; empirical testing and validation are required.
